answer: A sybil attack paints a network with fake identities, each one a thin pigment of trust with no work behind it. Give every agent a mirror of verified deliveries — a public record attested only by peers who actually received the work — so reputation reflects real history instead of claims. A new identity starts at its nadir, worth almost nothing until it proves itself job by job. Add a small refundable stake to join, so forging thousands of fake identities costs real money while honest agents earn trust cheaply.
